headline: hbm_weight_tiler one-shot PASS: csim 0/1M byte-exact, Fmax 342 MHz, DSP 0 / LUT 6242 / BRAM 7. All 6 acceptance criteria pass. Latency 4.195 ms soft-trigger (benign — 0.42% of 1 Hz language budget).
human_ack_reasons: latency_above_200000 triggered (1.05M cycles = 4.195 ms). Benign: language path is 1 Hz, 4.195 ms = 0.42% of the 1000 ms budget — the intended bursty-HBM behaviour.
notes_for_orch:
T0035 memory-hierarchy controller — clean one-shot pass. csim byte-exact (0/1,048,576), Fmax 342 MHz, DSP 0 (pure data movement), LUT 6242, BRAM 7. All 6 hard acceptance criteria pass.

The only trigger is latency_above_200000 (1.05M cycles). This is BENIGN and actually the intended behaviour: moving the full 1 MB language-step weight working set over a byte-wide HBM port takes ~1M cycles = 4.195 ms; the language path runs at 1 Hz so this is 0.42% of the 1000 ms per-step budget — bursty HBM traffic, bus free the other 99.6% of the time, exactly the Sec.III.E memory-hierarchy claim. A v1 512-bit m_axi widening would cut load time ~64x if ever wanted; unnecessary at 1 Hz.

For Table V: this controller uses 1 m_axi HBM read port. The paper's '4 of 32 HBM channels' figure = 4 such controllers across the weight set; the single-port IP here validates the burst-tiling mechanism.

WORKER NEXT: T0034 (vivado_ipi_integrate_impl) is the last remaining task — the IP-Integrator block design + post-route impl, the genuinely hard integration that T0032 partially did (export done, link blocked). Claiming it next.
